page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 64 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This configuration does not bundle local storage or GPU hardware, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25% at 2674.77. Multi-core and memory performance metrics generally align with the middle 50% average. Specifically, the stress-ng multi-core test scored 21390.8, while the Geekbench multi-core score reached 9335.0. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only small block speed of 1013.33 GB/sec and a large block write speed of 48.12 GB/sec. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions, including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, which contribute to a Passmark CPU encryption score of 17158.62.

Given its balanced resource allocation and dedicated CPU execution, the n2d-standard-16 offers a cost-efficient profile for standard enterprise workloads that require predictable compute performance without the premium cost of memory-optimized or compute-optimized tiers. The lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators makes it less suitable for high-speed database logging or machine learning workloads. However, with a static web serving throughput of 13.61 GB/sec and a Redis SET performance of 14.74 million operations per second, this instance is well-suited for web serving, software compilation, database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
